must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: Gender is the single strongest predictor of survival, with a statistically significant association ($\chi^2 = 263.05$, $p < 0.0001$).
must_find.reason: Report says sex is the dominant predictor but gives no survival rates or explicit direction that women survived more (only implied by 'Female + 1st Class yield the highest survival').

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.quote: Higher socioeconomic class (lower Pclass number) strongly correlates with survival.
must_find.reason: States survival is higher in higher classes, i.e. falls with class number, though without rates.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.reason: The report never compares fares between survivors and non-survivors.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: The high sparsity in 'Cabin' indicates that "No Cabin" is not just missing data but potentially an informative feature correlated with socioeconomic class.
must_find.reason: It links cabin missingness to class but never states that those without a cabin survived less often.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.reason: Age missingness is discussed only as an imputation matter, not in relation to survival.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.reason: Models are reported with accuracy but never compared with the 62% majority-class baseline.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.quote: Specific metrics like Precision, Recall, and F1-Score were noted as areas for deeper investigation in the task list but detailed numbers were truncated
must_find.reason: Report explicitly states that precision/recall/F1 results were not included.

must_not_claim.quote: The overall survival rate for the population was **38.38%** (342 survivors out of 891 passengers).
must_not_claim.reason: Report correctly says most did not survive.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.reason: Report never claims men survived more than women.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.quote: Higher socioeconomic class (lower Pclass number) strongly correlates with survival.
must_not_claim.reason: Report says higher class survived more, the opposite of the claim.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: Gender is the single strongest predictor of survival
must_not_claim.reason: Report names sex, not age, as strongest predictor, and ranks Age fourth.

caveats.quote: The 'Cabin' feature is highly sparse (77.10% missing), rendering standard imputation invalid.
caveats.reason: Report explicitly warns about missing Cabin data and its handling as a limitation.
